----- Reply (Ben provides technical plan)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Hi all — quick technical note on the seed approach we recommend for ephemeral auth:

1) We create a staging project in Redwood's infra and a project-scoped role "keystone-staging-inferencer" that has: generateTokens (sandbox), readModels, and limited quota.
2) Redwood will mint a short-lived service token via our token service API (ttl: configurable, default 1 hour). We will return a JSON payload with token metadata and a signed jwt for your secrets manager to consume.
3) Delivery options:
   - Option A (recommended): Push the token to a pre-provisioned ops-eng secret in your secrets manager via a secure webhook.
   - Option B: Provide an SFTP + GPG envelope where we deposit a one-time token file (less preferred).
4) KMS wrapping: we support you decrypting the envelope client-side using Google KMS keys. Provide the resource name and we will encrypt the payload with the public encryption key.

Acceptance tests we suggest:
- Use the staging token to call /v1/generate with a 512-token sample; validate latency < 350ms p50 and no auth errors.
- Confirm token rotation: request a fresh token after 45 minutes, ensure previous token invalidates.

I'll attach a short checklist and the API curl examples. Happy to run the script during tomorrow's screen share.

Ben Carter
Implementation Engineer, Redwood Inference
